summary: An on/off switch for a single setting, with its label, description and error laid out beside it, taking part in forms.

label.note: Visible label next to the switch and its accessible name. Required: shadow DOM keeps an external <label for> from reaching the inner control.

hideLabel.note: Visually hides the label; it stays the accessible name. Use only when the row has other visible text naming the setting.

description.note: Help text under the label: what turning the setting on does.

error.note: Error message. Setting it marks the field invalid and blocks form submission.

size.note: Track size: default 32x20 with a 16px thumb, sm 24x16 with a 12px thumb. The label text keeps its size.

value.note: Submitted with the form while the switch is on; nothing is submitted while off.

checked.note: Whether the switch is on. Not reflected: the attribute is the default restored by form reset.

required.note: Must be on for the form to submit (valueMissing while off). Adds an aria-hidden asterisk after the label.

disabled.note: Cannot be toggled or focused; dimmed; not submitted. A disabled ancestor fieldset has the same effect without changing this property.

anatomy.name: field
anatomy.notes: Grid: the switch in the first column, label, description and error in the second.

anatomy.name: control
anatomy.notes: The track: a pill that holds the thumb and the native input stretched over it.

anatomy.name: input
anatomy.notes: The focusable control exposed as a switch; receives focus, Space and validation. Covers the whole track so a click anywhere on it toggles.

anatomy.name: thumb
anatomy.notes: Round knob; sits at the inline start when off and the inline end when on (mirrored in right-to-left). Decorative, ignores the pointer.

anatomy.name: label
anatomy.notes: Native <label for> in the same shadow root; clicking it toggles.

anatomy.name: error
anatomy.notes: Persistent polite live region; text appears when invalid.

input.note: Each toggle by the user. Native and composed, so it crosses the shadow boundary. Not fired when checked is set in code.

change.note: Toggle committed by the user. Re-dispatched from the host because native change is not composed. Not fired when checked is set in code.

focus-visible.note: 3px solid ring around the track (a translucent ring would fall under 3:1).

checked.note: Track fills with the primary color and the thumb moves to the inline end; position, not color alone, tells on from off.

invalid.trigger: error set, or required and off after blur or a submit attempt

disabled.trigger: disabled attribute, or a disabled ancestor fieldset

accessibility.accessibleNameSource: The label prop, through a native <label for> in the same shadow root.

formAssociation.note: Form-associated custom element: submits value only while on; validity mirrored from the inner control (required -> valueMissing while off; error -> customError); form reset restores the default on/off state from the checked attribute; a disabled switch or one inside a disabled fieldset is not submitted, not focusable and skipped by validation; form state restore (back/forward cache, autofill) restores on/off.

accessibility.targetSize: Track 32x20 (sm 24x16). The label beside it is part of the clickable row and the 12px gap satisfies the WCAG 2.5.8 spacing exception; with hide-label the author must keep 24px of clear space around the track.
accessibility.focusRingVisible: On keyboard focus of the input; 3px ring in switch.focus-ring.color around the track.
accessibility.missingNameWarning: Dev-only console warning, once, when label is empty.

keyboard.Tab / Shift+Tab: move focus to and from the switch (skipped while disabled)
keyboard.Enter: submits the owning form (implicit submission, SB-0009); does not toggle

aria: role=switch on the native checkbox input; the on/off state is exposed as aria-checked true/false by the platform
aria-describedby -> description and error ids (same root)
required: native required on the input; the asterisk is aria-hidden
error: sets a customError validity, so the form blocks submission
no on/off text inside the track: the state is announced by the role, and the label must not change with the state
announcements: on/off state is announced on toggle by the switch role
error text is announced once when it appears (persistent aria-live=polite region)

useCases.when: A single setting that is either on or off, such as a preference in a settings form
useCases.use: sb-switch with a label that names the setting

useCases.when: What the setting does is not obvious from its name
A dense row (table, compact settings list)
The row already names the setting visibly (a table row, a card title)
useCases.use: hide-label, with the label still set

useCases.when: The setting must be on before the form can be sent
useCases.use: required, with an error that says why

antiPatterns.pattern: A switch that chooses between two named options (such as Monthly / Yearly)
antiPatterns.why: A switch reads as on/off for one thing; two named ends are ambiguous about which is on

antiPatterns.pattern: Several switches used to pick items from a list
antiPatterns.why: Selecting items is a choice recorded on submit, not a set of settings

antiPatterns.pattern: Accepting terms or giving consent with a switch
antiPatterns.why: Agreement is a choice, not a setting; a checkbox is the expected control

antiPatterns.pattern: A label that changes with the state ("Enabled" / "Disabled") or on/off text in the track
antiPatterns.why: The role already announces on/off; a changing name confuses screen-reader users and doubles the state
antiPatterns.alternative: A fixed label that names the setting

antiPatterns.pattern: A button that triggers an action, styled as a switch
antiPatterns.why: A switch has a persistent state; an action does not
antiPatterns.alternative: Button, or Toggle for a pressed state in a toolbar

drift.contract: label, description and error are props of Switch
drift.realization: shadcn composes Field and Label parts around Switch; shadow DOM requires them inside
shadcn uses input (neutral-200), below 3:1; changed for WCAG 1.4.11
shadcn uses 18.4px (1.15rem) and 14px; rounded to the size scale so thumb and inset are whole pixels

drift.contract: name, value, required, error and form reset
drift.realization: shadcn's Switch only mirrors a hidden input for name/value; required, reset and error are added here
not drawn by shadcn's Switch (it has aria-invalid styling only through Field)
not reflected: the attribute is the default restored by form reset

openQuestions.question: Contract content drafted with the contract-author skill (visual reference, WAI-ARIA APG)?
openQuestions.answer: Yes: APG Switch pattern (keyboard and role), the visual reference for look and sizes, the project's Checkbox for form behavior and layout.

openQuestions.question: Native <input type=checkbox role=switch> or a custom button with aria-checked?
openQuestions.answer: Native checkbox input with role=switch (recommended, SB-0007 native first): Space, required/valueMissing, label click and disabled come from the platform. A <button role=switch> was discarded because it needs all of those rebuilt by hand.

openQuestions.question: Does Enter toggle the switch?
openQuestions.answer: No. Space toggles; Enter submits the owning form like every other form control here (SB-0009). The APG lists Enter as optional for switches; toggling on Enter would make Enter behave differently on this one field of a form.

openQuestions.question: Is checked reflected to an attribute?
openQuestions.answer: No. As in Checkbox, the checked attribute is the default restored by form reset (like native defaultChecked); the checked property is the live state.

openQuestions.question: Sizes?
openQuestions.answer: default (32x20 track, 16px thumb) and sm (24x16 track, 12px thumb), from the existing size.switch.* semantic tokens. Named default/sm like the other controls (api.json size alias medium/small).

openQuestions.question: Where does the label go: after the switch, or before it with the switch at the row end?
openQuestions.answer: After the switch, in the same grid as Checkbox (switch first, label, description and error in the second column). A trailing switch for settings lists is left to a later layout prop or to Item composition.

openQuestions.question: Should a switch support required at all?
openQuestions.answer: Yes, as asked: required means the switch must be on (native valueMissing while off). The Usage section steers consent and agreement to Checkbox instead.

openQuestions.question: Does the thumb animate?
openQuestions.answer: Yes, a fast (150ms) slide, and no animation under prefers-reduced-motion.

openQuestions.question: Manual screen-reader pass (VoiceOver, NVDA) of on/off announcement and the required state.
